name: Brookhill
agent: Roseanne De Vere Hunt, Sherry FitzGerald Country Homes, Farms & Estates
questions: The price has dropped from €1.35m (Irish Times, June) to €1.2m after about five months on the market. Has there been any offer, and is the vendor open to an offer below €1.2m?

Brookhill is described as a protected structure. What exactly is on the Record of Protected Structures (main house only, or the coach house and gallery too), and are there any open planning conditions or works the council has asked for?
Is the ground-floor en-suite bedroom (4.6 × 3.8 m, with a 4.6 × 2.4 m en-suite) step-free from the gallery and the front door, and does its en-suite have a walk-in shower?
Where exactly does the brook run, and is it fenced from the lawns and paddocks? Has the house, yard or arena ever flooded?
What did oil cost over the last year, how old is the boiler, and when was the bio-cycle unit last serviced? BuyerIQ flags one critical finding for this Eircode: has a radon test been done?

ai.why: On fit it is close to ideal: a large ground-floor en-suite, four bathrooms and a town with schools 2 km away. But at €1.2m it is more than double the budget, and 14 acres with stables, an arena and a protected house on oil are a lot to maintain.

electricity.detail: Mains electricity, stated in the listing's services.

water.detail: Mains water, stated in the listing's services.

sewer.detail: Bio-cycle treatment unit, stated in the listing; ask its age and service history.

internet.detail: Fibre broadband, stated in the listing's services; BuyerIQ shows 103 Mb full fibre at E91 K021. Provider not confirmed.
internet.speed: ~103 Mb (full fibre; higher tiers likely available)

groundFloorBedroom.detail: Bedroom 2 (4.6 × 3.8 m) is on the ground floor of the converted coach house, with its own 4.6 × 2.4 m en-suite and a door to a private lawn, reached from the inner hallway by the utility room (per the floor plan).

type: Detached period house (late Georgian, protected structure)
bedsNote: Ground-floor en-suite bedroom in the coach house plus four doubles upstairs; a 4.7 × 3.87 m mezzanine study/library over the kitchen
heating: Oil-fired central heating with radiators; underfloor heating in the gallery and kitchen; Aga and a wood-burning stove
tagline: A late Georgian protected house joined by a 2004 glass gallery to a converted coach house, with stables, a barn and an arena on 14 acres, 2 km north-east of Fethard.

pros.text: A real ground-floor suite for the parents
pros.detail: Bedroom 2 in the coach house is 4.6 × 3.8 m with a 4.6 × 2.4 m en-suite and its own door to a lawn, away from the bedrooms upstairs.

pros.text: 14 acres with stables, a barn and an arena
pros.detail: 5.67 ha of lawns and stud-railed paddocks, four loose boxes, a 19 × 7.5 m barn, a workshop and a new 25 × 45 m fibre-surfaced arena; far more room than the dogs need.

pros.text: Room for six: 378 m², five doubles, four bathrooms
pros.detail: Three en-suites (ground-floor bedroom, main bedroom with dressing room, Bedroom 5) plus a family bathroom and a ground-floor WC; drawing and dining rooms plus an 8.1 × 4.7 m kitchen/dining and 4.7 × 3.0 m living area under a double-height roof.

pros.text: 2 km from Fethard, with schools in town
pros.detail: Holy Trinity NS (mixed, ~220 pupils) and Patrician Presentation (mixed secondary, ~280) are both on Rocklow Road in Fethard; Centra and Spar for daily shopping.
Tipperary University Hospital, Clonmel is about 14 km straight-line, and takes all ages 24 hours.

pros.text: Done up, mains water and fibre
pros.detail: Restored and extended in 2004 (architect James Montgomery), cosmetically updated since 2022; mains electricity and water and fibre broadband are stated (BuyerIQ: 103 Mb full fibre).

pros.text: Price already cut, long on the market
pros.detail: Launched at €1.35m (Irish Times, 18 June 2026), now €1.2m; listed 29 May, so about 150 days on the market. Room to negotiate.
The aerials show fields on all sides, a tree-lined drive and one neighbouring house and yard about 100 m east; BuyerIQ puts it outside mapped noise zones.

cons.detail: About €3,175/m² for 378 m², and 2.4× the usual €500k line; stamp duty about €14,000 (1% to €1m, 2% above).

cons.text: Protected structure, BER exempt, on oil
cons.detail: The Irish Times calls it a protected structure; no BER is published and heating is oil (radiators, with underfloor heating in the newer part), so a retrofit is limited by conservation rules and running costs are unknown.
14 acres of paddocks, stud-rail fencing, four stables, a barn, an arena, a vegetable garden and an old house; expect a groundskeeper or a lot of weekend work, or letting the land.
Thurles (about 24 km straight-line) has about 16 weekday trains to Heuston, roughly 1h10–1h35; Clonmel's station has no direct Dublin trains.

cons.text: Local schools are DEIS; strong ones are a drive
cons.detail: Holy Trinity NS and Patrician Presentation in Fethard are both DEIS with no readable ratings; Rockwell College (fee-paying, strong) is about 15 km away near Cashel.
The Irish Times says a brook runs along the boundary; with two small boys and dogs, check where it runs and whether it floods.

cons.text: Most bedrooms are upstairs, in two wings
cons.detail: Four of the five bedrooms are on the first floor; Bedrooms 4 and 5 are reached along a corridor in the rear wing, and the library is on a mezzanine up a stair.
